title: Catalog API pagination contract decision
purpose: Document the two competing, unapproved drafts for GET /v1/items pagination and record that the authoritative contract remains unselected.

scope.text: Two competing drafts exist for GET /v1/items pagination: a cursor-based draft with an items array and next_cursor string, and a page/page_size draft returning a top-level JSON array.

requirements.text: Catalog API draft A: GET /v1/items returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string.
UI must support moving to the next page.
Catalog API draft B: GET /v1/items returns a top-level JSON array and uses page and page_size query parameters.

stories.text: If a human selects draft A as the authoritative contract, a client can request GET /v1/items and the UI can move to the next page.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected draft A as the authoritative contract, when a client calls GET /v1/items, then the response is a JSON object containing an items array and a next_cursor string.
Given a human has selected draft A as the authoritative contract, when the UI moves to the next page, then that page transition is supported.

stories.text: If a human selects draft B as the authoritative contract, a client can request GET /v1/items using page and page_size query parameters.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected draft B as the authoritative contract, when a client calls GET /v1/items with page and page_size query parameters, then the response is a top-level JSON array.

edge_cases.text: A request that combines one draft's paging mechanism with the other draft's response shape is not covered by either supplied draft; such a combination would need a human decision before it is treated as in scope.

dependencies.text: Neither draft is approved; the authoritative contract has not been selected.

risks.text: Implementing draft A's items-array-plus-next_cursor response and paging would not satisfy draft B's top-level array with page and page_size parameters, and implementing draft B would not satisfy draft A; satisfying one draft leaves the other unmet.

success_metrics.text: After a human selects an authoritative contract, verify the implemented GET /v1/items response shape and paging parameters against the selected draft only.

open_questions: Which draft is authoritative for GET /v1/items: draft A (items array with next_cursor) or draft B (top-level array with page and page_size)?
Who has authority to select the authoritative catalog API contract?
If draft A is selected, what response shape and behavior are required for the final page where next_cursor is absent or empty?
If draft B is selected, how are page and page_size validated and defaulted?
